Emma —

Thanks for the note and the profile. Quick summary below you can forward to finance/procurement. I’ll also attach a short SOW and a price sheet.

1) Efficiency math (batching + KV cache) — ballpark impact on per-token unit economics
   - Baseline: no batching, no KV cache (per-token cost = baseline unit)
   - Moderate batching (continuous batching, small latency SLO bump): ~15–25% token cost reduction for chat workloads with median seq len < 512.
   - KV/prefix cache (saves repeated prompt prefixes + long contexts): additional 10–30% reduction depending on prefix hit rate. In your profile the prefix hit rate looked ~35%, expect ~8–12% net savings from caching.
   - Combined conservative estimate for PivotalBank: 20–35% cost reduction from runtime optimizations. We model end-to-end effects in the attached pricing sheet.

2) Quantization recommendations and quality tradeoffs
   - Quant tiers we commonly use: FP16 (default hosted), Q4_0/Q4_1 (safe quant), Q5/Q6 (aggressive) — each step down reduces memory and compute.
   - For retrieval-augmented chat with regulatory logging, we recommend starting on Q4_1 for pilot (very low regressions) and moving to Q5 only after evals against your 200 prompt test set.
   - We offer a regression-detection run as part of Optimize that flags output-score drift vs your golden prompt set. If you want, Kimberly can run an initial pass on your test set.

3) Commercial offers (pilot -> commit)
   - Pilot: 3-month pilot, up to $6k in platform credits + discounted compute (15% off list) for anything burnt during pilot.
   - Commit: 12-month reserved commitment tiers — we can offer a stepped rebate structure up to 25% off list depending on committed TUs and an efficiency credit for expected batching/caching savings (structured as monthly bill credits, not a lower list price).
   - Net example: with a 12-month commit sized to your projected Q3 run-rate, combined with expected runtime savings, net effective unit cost could drop ~30% relative to list price.

4) Next steps and docs
   - Attached: short SOW draft and a pricing sheet with worked examples for your profile.
   - Kimberly: can kick off an evaluation run against the 200 prompt set and provide recommended quant profiles + a short regression report.

If procurement wants a formal commercial term (SLA, data controls), Connor can prep the contract path. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,

Emma / Marcus — quick technical notes from my side on the sample you sent:

- Observations: median seq len ~ 420, tail to ~2k (session transcripts). This profile benefits materially from prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and user history. Hitting a 35% cache hit rate (as Marcus estimated) is reasonable after a couple weeks of steady usage.

- Batching guidance: aim for an adaptive batching window (0–50ms) on user-facing L1 endpoints to preserve p95 latency. For background L2 batch jobs (batch rerank, embeddings refresh) we recommend larger windows to maximize throughput.

- Quant strategy (practical steps):
  1) Pilot on Q4_1 for all production-intent models — runs on your latency SLO should be acceptable and quant regressions minimal.
  2) Run A/B eval with Q5 on the 200 prompts with both automatic metrics and 40 human checks we can help run. If delta <0.8 points on your primary metric, we can greenlight a gradual rollout.
  3) If you move to aggressive quant (Q5+), we'll require a rollback plan and an enforced monitoring hook in the Console to auto-fall back on quality thresholds.

- Deliverables I can commit to during the pilot: one regression report, token-level latency/cost breakdowns per endpoint, and a short runbook for cache-warming and batching settings.

Happy to run the initial eval this week if you share the 200 prompt set and a sample of your logs (anonymized).

—Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
